title: Standardized Financial Analytics Environment
business: A global financial analytics firm managing heterogeneous cloud and on-premises infrastructure.
problem: The firm suffers from configuration drift where analytics engines deployed on AWS EC2 differ from those on local VMware clusters, leading to inconsistent calculation results and difficult debugging cycles.
solution: Packer enables the firm to define a single HCL configuration that acts as a source of truth, triggering parallel builds to generate platform-specific artifacts like AMIs for AWS and VMDK files for VMware from the same base image definition.
steps: Define a base HCL template specifying the OS and necessary analytics dependencies.
Configure builders for both AWS and VMware within the same template file.
Execute the build process to trigger parallel image creation across providers.
Validate the resulting artifacts against the firm's security compliance baseline.
outcome: The firm achieves environment parity, ensuring that analysts work on identical software stacks regardless of the underlying infrastructure provider, which simplifies maintenance and reduces deployment errors.
limitation: Packer creates static machine images, meaning that any change to the underlying software requires a full rebuild of the image; verify this by checking the build timestamp of the artifact against the current version control commit hash.

questions.question: In Standardized Financial Analytics Environment, what is the primary benefit of using Packer to address configuration drift?
options: It allows for the creation of identical machine images for multiple platforms from a single source configuration.
It replaces existing configuration management tools like Chef or Puppet entirely.
It provides real-time performance monitoring for running virtual machines.
It automatically migrates existing virtual machines between different cloud providers.
questions.explanation: The scenario highlights that the firm suffers from configuration drift, and Packer solves this by using a single source configuration to create identical images across platforms.
questions.evidence: Packer enables the firm to define a single HCL configuration that acts as a source of truth, triggering parallel builds to generate platform-specific artifacts like AMIs for AWS and VMDK files for VMware from the same base image definition.

questions.question: In Standardized Financial Analytics Environment, what is a key limitation of the image-based approach?
options: Images cannot be stored in version control systems.
Any change to the underlying software requires a full rebuild of the image.
Packer cannot build images for VMware and AWS simultaneously.
The resulting images are not compatible with standard cloud providers.
questions.explanation: Because Packer produces static images, updates require a new build cycle rather than live patching.
